correctness.rationale: The finite Esakia upset algebra uses the incidence height-two order and the specified forward relation xRz iff strict vertex-edge incidence or marked reflexive loop. Alvarez Definition 3.10 and Theorem 3.15 identify congruences order-dually with closed archival upsets, all subsets being closed in finite discrete topology. For an unmarked edge e, an archival upset contains e only if it contains both endpoints: a missing endpoint x has no possible witness y in S above x with yRe unless e has a loop, which it does not. Upsetness gives the converse. Therefore vertex selection is constant on connected components of the unmarked-edge graph. For a marked edge e, membership is forced if any endpoint is selected but freely optional otherwise, with y=e as archival witness; marked vertex loops yield no new obligations. Passing to quotient components produces exactly upsets of the incidence poset I(Q) with loop/parallel edge tokens intact. Order reversal/complement yields Con(A) isomorphic to Down(I(Q)); choosing absent quotient vertices W gives sum_W 2^|E(Q[W])|. Independent direct quantified archival enumeration agreed with quotient counts for every graph and edge-loop marking on n=0,1,2,3,4 (cases 1,1,3,27,729; total 761), with no extrapolation of finite tests to general n.
